goal: Adds a dedicated CI workflow that runs full Guix release builds for Linux, Windows and macOS on every PR and push.
Aims to catch reproducible-build breakage and codesign-manifest errors before they surface at release time.
reviewability: Ready. Author marked it ready for review and the only open item is a design question about relying on two self-operated substitute servers, which does not block reviewing the current code.
agreement: Positive. fanquake and sedited gave Concept ACK, and hebasto reviewed a prior commit in depth and got the author to align with the overlapping #35929 approach (willcl-ark).

categories.name: build
why: P2 because it strengthens release integrity by exercising the actual Guix reproducible-build pipeline (including a new codesign-environment check) on every PR instead of only at release time.
It doesn't fix a currently broken build, so it stops short of P1, but it materially reduces the chance of shipping a broken or non-reproducible release binary.

result.summary: This PR adds a new GitHub Actions workflow that runs the project's Guix release build for arm64-apple-darwin, x86_64-linux-gnu and x86_64-w64-mingw32 on pull requests and pushes, with caching for the Guix bootstrap, time-machine checkouts, depends sources/builds and the macOS SDK. It also adds a small install-guix.sh helper and exposes the pinned time-machine URL/commit from the Guix prelude so other scripts (and a substitute-build server) can reuse them. A third commit adds a lightweight codesign-manifest check that builds (but does not sign) the Windows and macOS codesign environments to catch manifest or dependency errors early.
result.problem: Guix reproducible builds and the codesign manifest are currently only exercised manually or at release time, so breakage (missing imports, broken dependencies, non-reproducibility) can go unnoticed until a release is being cut, which is costly for release managers and risks shipping a bad binary.

open_concerns: Author's own open question: whether the project should rely on two self-operated substitute servers as the only enabled substitute sources for these jobs, or add the slower upstream default servers, or find another server operator (willcl-ark).
resolved_concerns: hebasto found the first commit's approach to caching duplicated #35929's solution and only partially fixed the underlying duplicate-build issue; willcl-ark agreed to drop that commit and align with/rebase on #35929 instead.

categories.name: build
categories.evidence: The PR adds a new CI workflow (.github/workflows/guix.yml), an install script, and prelude changes specifically to run Guix reproducible builds and codesign-manifest checks in CI, squarely matching the build category's coverage of Guix builds and CI configuration.
categories.rationale: P2 because it moves Guix release-build and codesign-manifest verification into routine CI instead of leaving it to manual or release-time checks, directly serving the category's top priority of release integrity. The author notes this is meant 'to catch manifest errors and broken dependencies without requiring signatures or signing keys' (commit message), which reduces the chance of discovering reproducibility or signing problems only at release time. It stops short of P1 because it is not fixing an active regression or supported-platform breakage today, and reliance on two self-operated substitute servers is still an open operational question the author flags himself.

uncertainties: Whether the reliance on the author's personally-operated substitute servers as the sole substitute source is acceptable to the wider project long-term is unresolved, which could affect how the workflow is finally configured but not the priority of having Guix CI at all.

Overlap with #35929 and the closed #36006/#35855 conflicting PRs suggests some further consolidation may still be needed before merge, though this is a process/rebase matter rather than a reviewability blocker as of the latest activity.
result.card: This PR adds a standalone GitHub Actions workflow that runs the project's Guix release build (Linux, Windows, macOS) plus a lightweight codesign-manifest check on every PR and push, aiming to catch reproducibility and signing-dependency breakage before release rather than only when cutting a release. The author states the codesign check exists 'to catch manifest errors and broken dependencies without requiring signatures or signing keys.' fanquake and sedited gave Concept ACK, and an earlier substantive concern from hebasto about duplicating caching work done in #35929 was resolved when the author agreed to drop the overlapping commit. The PR is marked ready for review; the author's own remaining open question is whether the project should rely solely on his two self-operated Guix substitute servers, an operational choice rather than a code-review blocker. It conflicts with two other open Guix time-machine update PRs (#36233, #35855) and overlaps with #35929, suggesting some coordination is still needed before merge.
